# Best rechargeable AA batteries (NiMH)

**Best overall: Panasonic Eneloop Pro (high-drain devices)**
- Digital Camera World's tester names it best overall and has used it for years in flash testing ([Digital Camera World](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries)). GearLab also picks it, at about $17.99 for a 4-pack ([GearLab](https://gearlab.io/best-rechargeable-batteries-for-household-devices/)).
- It holds about 85% of its charge after a year of storage, and it comes pre-charged ([GearLab](https://gearlab.io/best-rechargeable-batteries-for-household-devices/)).
- The tradeoff is that Pro cells are rated for fewer recharge cycles than standard Eneloops, in exchange for higher capacity (about 2,450-2,500 mAh minimum) ([GearLab](https://gearlab.io/best-rechargeable-batteries-for-household-devices/)).
- The results didn't include a direct buy link. The Digital Camera World guide links to Adorama, Amazon and Newegg: https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries

**Best budget: IKEA LADDA**
- Charge-Test's review says LADDA cells are almost certainly Eneloop-made (IKEA hasn't confirmed this), and the 2450 mAh version matches the Eneloop Pro rating ([Charge-Test](https://charge-test.com/ikea-ladda-batteries-review-still-the-best-budget-aa-aaa-rechargeable-in-2026/)).
- The IKEA US page I have lists the **1900 mAh** LADDA at **$9.99 for 4**, rated 4.7/5 from 1,009 reviews: [IKEA LADDA AA](https://www.ikea.com/us/en/p/ladda-rechargeable-battery-hr06-aa-1-2v-00509814/)
- GearLab lists the 2450 mAh version at $7.99, but Charge-Test's €7.99 price is for Europe, so I couldn't confirm that price or availability in the US. Check IKEA's site or your local store.

**Best in bulk: Tenergy Premium PRO, 2,800 mAh**
- A 20-pack is $42.99 (about $2.15 per cell). Tenergy lists 1,200 cycles and 85% charge retention after a year ([Dealectric listing](https://dealectric.com/tenergy-premium-pro-aa-2800mah-20-pack)).
- That listing is from an affiliate site, and its buy button is an affiliate link. The specs come from Tenergy's own page.
- The warranty is unclear: 12 months on the product page, but 90 days on Tenergy's warranty page. Returns cost you shipping.
- Be a little skeptical of the 2,800 mAh figure. One lab test found inflated ratings on a different brand's 2,800 mAh cells, which held up poorly under heavy load ([Frame & Focal](https://frameandfocal.com/camera-reviews/which-aa-rechargeable-battery-gives-you-the-best-bang-for-your-buck)). I have no independent test of the Tenergy cells.

**Low-drain only: Amazon Basics High-Capacity**
- GearLab suggests it for clocks and remotes ($12.99 for 8) ([GearLab](https://gearlab.io/best-rechargeable-batteries-for-household-devices/)). Frame & Focal's tests found it faded much faster than Eneloop Pro over a year of heavy use ([Frame & Focal](https://frameandfocal.com/camera-reviews/which-aa-rechargeable-battery-best-after-one-year-abuse-440920)). I'd skip it for cameras, flashes or flashlights.

**Things to know**
- NiMH cells are 1.2 V, not 1.5 V. A few devices built strictly for alkalines may read them as low. Digital Camera World also covers 1.5 V lithium-ion AAs for those cases.
- Some of these sources have inconsistent numbers, so treat exact prices and test figures as approximate.

**My pick:** Eneloop Pro for cameras, flashes and controllers, or IKEA LADDA if you want the best value and live near an IKEA. Tell me your device and I can narrow it down, or suggest a charger.
